newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs hit '97 high on liquidity-driven buying.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs hit '97 high on liquidity-driven buying.

text.p: South Korean stocks rose 1.54 percent to a new yearly high in Friday's mid-morning session on liquidity-driven buying, brokers said.
The composite index was up 1.54 percent, or 11.95 points, to 786.61 at 0110 GMT. Construction firms led the gains on hopes that recent drops in interest rates would boost their earnings.
The construction sector's sub-index soared 6.71 percent, or 20.24 points, to 321.69 points by 0120 GMT. Many construction firms rose by their daily limits of eight percent.
Brokers said the liquidity was high mainly because financial institutions have tightened credits to companies since a series of corporate collapses rocked the financial industry.
The benchmark three-year corporate bonds are currently trading below 11.50 percent, compared with 12.60 percent at the end of 1996, bond market dealers said.
